tagline.text: An afternoon of song and lunch on an emerald river

children.text: A green river flowing through lush palm forest in inland Bohol, famous for a river cruise where floating restaurants serve a buffet lunch with live music. Sitting on the road to the Chocolate Hills, it's a fixture on the lunch stop of any Bohol countryside tour.

The Loboc River rises in the mountains of central Bohol, flows through Loboc town, and empties into the Bohol Sea at Loay to the south. Coconut, nipa palm, and bamboo grow thick along both banks, and where the water has passed through limestone terrain, it takes on a deep emerald color on a clear day. About
40 minutes
from Tagbilaran by car, right on the main road to the Chocolate Hills, it's rarely left out of a Bohol countryside tour.

What made the Loboc River famous is its floating restaurant cruise. Raft-boats built with two banana-boat-shaped hulls topped with a roof and dining tables move slowly upriver while passengers eat a Filipino buffet lunch and listen to live singing accompanied by guitar and keyboard. Partway along, riverside villagers put on a stage show of traditional dance and song, and the boat turns back near a small waterfall upstream (Busay Falls).

In the riverside village of Loboc stands the Church of San Pedro Apostol, built by the Jesuits in the 17th century. Considered one of the oldest churches in Bohol, it was heavily damaged in the magnitude-7.2 Bohol earthquake of
but reopened in
after a long restoration. The village is also known as the hometown of the Loboc Children's Choir, winner of several international choir competitions.

The Loboc River cruise is quiet and physically undemanding, making it especially well suited to family trips with parents or young children. More active travelers can enjoy the same river in a completely different mood with an early-morning stand-up paddleboard (SUP) session or a nighttime firefly tour.
Departing from the pier at the Loboc Tourism Complex, the boat makes a round trip upriver over about
1 hour
. It includes a Filipino-style buffet of rice, fish, chicken adobo, vegetables, and fruit, plus live music, with departures throughout
10:00 AM to 3:00 PM

Partway through the cruise, the boat briefly pulls up to a bamboo stage on the riverbank, where locals perform traditional dances such as tinikling with bamboo poles, along with songs. A small tip or souvenir purchase may be encouraged after the show.
At the upstream turning point of the cruise is a broad, low, stepped waterfall, letting you take in the white spray and green forest up close.

Right beside the pier, the Church of San Pedro Apostol has an impressive stone facade restored after earthquake damage and striking ceiling paintings inside. The view of the river from the bridge in front of the church is also worthwhile.

Operators upstream run stand-up paddleboard tours that start early in the morning before the cruise boats begin running, letting you enjoy the quiet river and birdsong. Beginners can join after a short lesson.
There are tours by boat or SUP after dark to see fireflies gathering in the mangroves and trees along the river. They're especially visible on moonless nights and toward the end of the rainy season.
About
15 minutes
from Loboc toward the Chocolate Hills, Sevilla has a hanging bridge woven from bamboo over the river — a good brief stop during a countryside tour.

The most common approach is to charter a countryside tour vehicle. Starting from Panglao, a car runs about
and can cover the Chocolate Hills and the Tarsier Sanctuary in the same day. Tour packages often include the cruise lunch, so confirm this when booking.
The river is at its clearest emerald when rain is scarce, during
December–May
February–April
especially has clear skies that make the river's color and the forest's green stand out vividly. Midday is hot, but the cruise boats have a roof and a river breeze, so it's bearable.
During the rainy season,
June–November

, soil washed down from upstream often turns the river brown, and after heavy rain the water level can rise enough to halt cruises. Check whether the cruise is running that day if a typhoon has passed through or a heavy rain warning is in effect. Fireflies are relatively plentiful toward the end of the rainy season and in early dry season.
During Holy Week, the Christmas holidays, and Korean holiday periods, tour groups crowd in and the ticket line lengthens between
11:00 AM and 1:00 PM
. Taking the first boat around
or going after
is much more relaxed.

items.label: Buffet lunch river cruise
items.note: About 1 hour, includes buffet and performance

children.text: Prices are approximate as of
and may vary depending on local conditions.
Most people visit the Loboc River as a day trip, but there are a few bamboo-and-wood lodges and bungalows along the riverbank worth an overnight stay. Prices run about
a night, and many lack air conditioning, so confirm when booking. If you want amenities, it's more common to base yourself on Panglao Island or in Tagbilaran city and visit for the day.

The cruise buffet is unassuming Filipino home cooking — rice, grilled fish, chicken and pork adobo, pancit (stir-fried noodles), stir-fried vegetables, and fruit like mango and banana. It's best thought of as a meal for the atmosphere more than the food. Around Loboc village, shops sell Bohol specialty snacks such as calamay, buko pie, and ube halaya, and buying buko juice (fresh coconut juice) from a stall in front of the church is also a treat.
The pier ticket booth runs mainly on cash. Loboc has few ATMs, so bring cash from Tagbilaran or Panglao.
Since several cruise boats run almost the same route, sitting at a railing seat facing the river gives you the best view of the scenery. Boarding earlier works in your favor for seat choice.
The buffet line gets long right after departure, so it's more comfortable to enjoy the scenery for the first
10 minutes
and then get your food at a slower pace.
During the rainy season, whether the cruise runs can be decided the morning of. Check with your tour driver or accommodation ahead of time.
SUP and firefly tours have limited capacity and need booking at least a day ahead. Bring a waterproof bag and a change of clothes.
Good photo spots are the view of the river from the bridge beside the church, in front of Busay Falls, and the riverside bamboo performance stage.
There are a lot of mosquitoes, so bring long clothing and repellent, especially for evening tours.
The cruise fare includes the buffet lunch, but drinks are usually extra. Bring some small cash if you want bottled water or soda.
After heavy rain in the rainy season, the river level rises quickly and the current gets strong. During this period, don't swim or SUP in the river, and follow the operators' instructions.
Don't lean on the cruise boat's railing or stand at the bow for photos. The boat rocks when it turns.
Littering or throwing food into the river is prohibited.
Catching fireflies or shining a flashlight on them reduces their numbers. Observe quietly only.
Inside the church, covering your shoulders and knees is customary, and you should refrain from tourist photography during Mass.
Some people take photos of you at the pier and on the boat and then quote an inflated price of
or more for the prints or files. If you don't want them, politely decline from the start, and if you do plan to buy, confirm the price first.
